I had a few other outfits on hand, the clothes fit any girl Animator. My friend is a collector, and I’m a doll rehabber, lol, so I figured she might want Meg as a thank you. She declined.

At the bus station, a guy helped me haul the suitcase out of the trunk of my Uber, we joked about how heavy doll bodies could be. On the bus, I got lucky that I had two seats to myself. A mom and her daughter, maybe eight or nine, sit across from me. The kid across the aisle from me, Emma, borrows a notebook, shares my food, borrows my hoodie when she’s cold—her mom said it was fine when I checked with her before handing anything over.

About an hour in, Emma reaches over and picks up my sketch book. I take it back, tell her that’s not polite, and put it in my bag. A little bit later she reaches over, *into my bag*, and takes my tablet. I take it back, tell her it’s not a good habit to help yourself to other people’s things, and put it away. This time the bag goes to my other side in the window seat. She pouts, but that’s the end of it. Next stop, she asks to borrow my tablet and settles into watching a movie. I got out with everyone else and notice the guy that had helped me with my suitcase is sitting on a bench with his daughter, doing a birthday cupcake with a candle from the mini-mart. I overhear that her name is Selena and she’s five.

So I hop back on the bus, grab Meg and her accessories out of my carry-on, write a quick *Happy Birthday Selena* on a slip of paper, and left Meg sitting on her seat. I ducked back out, snagged her Dad to let him know it was me, and go about my business.

When I get back on the bus, Selena is sobbing, Meg in her arms like she’d been handed the Hope diamond. I faked the surprised reaction, blending in with everyone else on the bus that’s trying to console her, but she’s just so happy- it was a moment. Nobody outed me, praise the Fates.

At our last stop, as we’re all getting off the bus, Emma’s mom pulled me aside and said it was really shitty of me to give Selena the doll when her daughter was sitting right next to me the whole time. Emma had shown zero interest in the doll when it was sitting next to me in my bag; she’d never asked about it.

I snapped at her about how I could calculate the cost of letting her kid use my tablet, fed her, loaned her my clothing, paid attention to her and played babysitter the entire bus ride while you slept on the window--and it still wouldn’t cover the cost of the hair alone. I told her to back the fuck up and mind her own business, who I give or sell my dolls to is at my discretion.
